reasoning: I accept the Market Analyst's risk-on lean, but only as the low-conviction call it is (confidence 0.4). Breadth, credit and volatility do not confirm a broad selloff, while tech momentum and the near-certain December hike argue against it. I approve one small rotation. P1 sells MSM in full, and P2 buys INCY at $15 instead of $17. Health Care is the Market Analyst's top favored sector, and INCY was my named next candidate. The account is 88.5% invested, and the owner wants cash put to work. Lessons: L2 (INCY's date is verified from filings: reported 10-29, next 2027-02-09). L3 (INCY overlaps IDXX, so Health Care goes to about 10.5% and I size for that; FAST and MSM count as one sleeve). L4 (at about 2.4% of equity INCY is not a token buy, and it follows a stated tilt rather than diversification alone). L6 and L7 (stored text rewritten, see below). The Skeptic's serious data objection to INCY is fair: the Q3 content is not in the packet and there is no INCY price series. Two things answer it. Twelve sessions of news coverage since the 10-29 print show no guidance cut, 4.02 or 5.02. And the trimmed size keeps a $2.5 cushion over the 10% cash buffer, which the Implicator flagged as thin at $17. Every held stop shows 'missing', so all 14 get a numeric stop_price in thesis_updates, taken from the level each invalidation already states. VOO and VTI use stop_on SPY at the 200-day level of 728.3 (11-10). Two stops change on purpose. I re-anchor WMT from about $110 (7% under entry) to $116. The Skeptic is right that an 11.8% position going into an approximate 11-19 print after five PT raises is exposed. No trim was proposed, so a tighter stop is the lever I have. I also replace IEF's unmeasurable 'yields materially higher' clause with a 200-day test. Qualitative clauses were checked after the 11-10 hot CPI, and none has tripped. BND: the Market Analyst is risk-on, but TLT is 2.30% and IEF 1.24% below their 200-day averages, both short of 3%. VNQ: TLT is not 3% below its 200-day, and real estate is not avoided. IEF: there has been no Fed outcome since 10-28, and IEF is only -0.16% over 5 days. VOO: RSP's 21-day return is +3.61%, still positive. WMT: XLP's 21-day return is +7.84%, well above +3%, and there is no guidance cut. DPZ: the guidance-cut item is nine sessions old with no filing, so I treat it as nothing, and DPZ stays on the menu with CFO above net income. KR: the cyber item is unconfirmed. IDXX: up about 25% since the 10-20 fill against XLV's +9.8% over 21 days, so it is not lagging. CARG, MSCI, MSM, VRSN and FAST have no new 8-K or guidance cut. Holdings review: I agree with every hold and with selling MSM. Three caveats. On FAST against MSM, the Skeptic is right that MSM has the stronger fundamentals. I keep FAST for its lower vol (0.245 against 0.327) and beta (0.515 against 0.824) in a sector the Market Analyst avoids, so this is a risk call, not a quality one. On IEF, I take the Skeptic's direction case seriously but there is no sell proposal. The measurable clause should decide it, and IEF is the first bond to cut if cash is needed. On VTI, I doubt the proposer's 'slight edge over SPY'. I hold it as core beta, not as an expected outperformer.

trades.thesis: Consolidate the industrial MRO sleeve into FAST. MSM duplicates FAST's business, and the Market Analyst lists Industrials under avoid. At 1.3% of equity it adds nothing FAST does not. FAST is kept for its lower vol and beta, not for better fundamentals: MSM is F9 with CFO 1.38x net income, and the Skeptic is right on that. The sale realizes a negligible short-term gain (about $0.10) with no wash-sale issue, and the proceeds go toward a favored sector.
trades.invalidation: Over the next 20 sessions MSM beats both SPY and INCY by more than 3 percentage points, or the Market Analyst moves Industrials from avoid to favor.

trades.thesis: Quality Health Care name in the Market Analyst's top favored sector: F8, gp_sector_pct 0.906, CFO $1,413.5M against net income $1,286.7M, vol 0.330, beta 0.456. It reported 10-29 and the next earnings date is 2027-02-09. No 4.01, 4.02 or 5.02 has been filed since, and the only news is small pipeline items. It overlaps held IDXX in Health Care, but the businesses differ (oncology drugs against animal diagnostics), and the size keeps the bucket near 10.5%. Resized from $17 to $15 for two reasons. The Skeptic is right that the packet has neither the Q3 content nor INCY's own price trend. And the smaller size keeps a cushion over the 10% cash buffer. Single-name biotech risk (trial readouts, regulation) is larger than beta suggests.
